key_insight: Detonation-sprayed titanium dioxide-based coatings can be tuned for roughness, thickness, and hydrophobicity by adjusting process parameters, with clear mathematical relationships between surface properties and spraying conditions.
engineering_relevance: This work provides practical process windows and predictive equations for optimizing coating performance in wear-resistant, corrosion-resistant, and hydrophobic surface engineering applications.
method: Varied detonation spraying parameters, especially nozzle passage speed and spray distance.
Measured coating surface roughness, thickness, and contact angle to assess hydrophobicity.
Derived empirical laws linking roughness/thickness to nozzle speed and roughness/contact angle to spray distance.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimental observation of parameter-dependent surface properties and new equations that fit inverse power and parabolic trends for predicting coating behavior.
watch_item: The conclusions appear based on a specific TiO2-based coating system, so the equations and optimal settings may not transfer directly to other materials or spray setups without recalibration.
paper_title: Surface Characteristics of Titanium Based Coatings Obtained by Detonation Spraying Under Various Process Conditions
